name: Carsi (Old Town)
tagline: The UNESCO heart among Ottoman mansions
description: The historic core in the valley, where cobbled lanes wind between timber konak mansions, the covered Arasta bazaar, old hammams and mosques. It is the most atmospheric and tourist-facing part of town, packed with guesthouses, sweet shops and craft workshops.
bestFor: Heritage lovers wanting to live inside the postcard, steps from cafes and bazaar

name: Kirankoy
tagline: The newer upper town for daily life
description: The modern district above the old town, where more locals actually live and shop. It offers everyday amenities, banks, markets and ordinary flats, plus cafes with wifi. Less picturesque than Carsi but more practical for a longer, grounded stay.
bestFor: Nomads wanting everyday convenience, amenities and a real local base over scenery
cons: A walk or ride down to Carsi

name: Baglar
description: The traditional summer-house area spread across green, breezy hillsides above town. Larger garden mansions and orchards give it a relaxed, spacious feel, cooler in high summer. It is residential and calm, better for peace and views than for nightlife or convenience.
bestFor: Slow-base nomads wanting gardens, cool air and views away from crowds

name: Incekaya and Canyon Edge
tagline: Toward the aqueduct, canyon and Karabuk
description: The outer stretch northwest of town toward the Incekaya aqueduct and Tokatli canyon, blending countryside with the road to Karabuk and its train station. It is scenic and outdoorsy, ideal for walkers, though you rely on taxis or dolmus to reach the centre.
bestFor: Nature lovers wanting canyon walks, viewpoints and easy transport links to Karabuk
pros: Great for hikes and fresh air
cons: Far from cafes and the old town
Needs a car, taxi or dolmus
